title: IT Act s. 45 — Capital Gains (Short-term & Long-term) (IT Act s. 45)

content.overview: Section 45 charges profits or gains arising from the transfer of a capital asset as capital gains in the year of transfer. A capital asset is property of any kind, with the exclusions in section 2(14). Transfer is defined in section 2(47). Short-term and long-term depend on the holding period. The computation is full value less cost of acquisition and improvement and transfer expenses. The charge needs a capital asset and a transfer. A business stock-in-trade is not a capital asset.

enhancement.legalPrinciple: The charge needs a capital asset and a transfer. A business stock-in-trade is not a capital asset.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 45 is the charge. Exemptions in sections 54 and following remove gains that meet those investment conditions. Slump sale, compulsory acquisition and specified conversions have their own timing. The holding period that divides short-term and long-term is statutory and is not frozen here. Indexation applies only where the computation section allows it.
examples: Land held as an investment is transferred.
The same land held as stock by a dealer is business income.
A residential-house exemption is a section 54 question, not part of the charge.
